original_assignment_row.description_short: Trump Moved the Forest Service Out of Washington in Another Attack on Scientists Who Wouldn't Play Along
original_assignment_row.description_medium: The Guardian reported that Trump's administration would move the US Forest Service headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City, reviving a familiar relocation tactic critics described as an attack on science and scientists. The cruelty here is managerial rather than theatrical. Shift the office, shred the continuity, and watch experienced staff disappear while calling the self-inflicted hollowing-out a commonsense efficiency measure.
original_assignment_row.description_long: The Guardian reported on March 31, 2026, that the Agriculture Department planned to move the U.S. Forest Service headquarters from Washington, D.C., to Salt Lake City and close its regional offices. The announcement put into motion a reorganization officials had been planning since the prior year. USDA described the move as a “commonsense approach,” while critics called it an attack on science and scientists. The report compared it with the first Trump administration’s relocation of the Bureau of Land Management from Washington to Colorado. Nearly 90 percent of the BLM’s Washington-based staff declined to move, and the agency later returned to Washington under President Biden. That history helps explain concerns that relocation could disrupt staffing and institutional knowledge, but it does not establish how many Forest Service employees would leave or whether the same outcome would occur. The announcement described a planned headquarters move and regional-office closures; it did not say the change had already been completed or that scientists were being punished for refusing to support administration policy.

original_assignment_row.description_short: Trump: RFK appoints quack to vaccine safety office
original_assignment_row.description_medium: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hired Lyn Redwood in June 2025 for an HHS role whose exact scope was not announced. ABC News reported that Redwood was expected to present on thimerosal at a vaccine-advisory meeting. original_assignment_row.description_long: In June 2025, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hired Lyn Redwood, although the department did not identify her exact role. ABC News reported that Redwood was expected to present at an Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices meeting about thimerosal, a preservative still used in some flu vaccines but removed from routine childhood vaccines in 2001. Her planned presentation cited a 2008 rat study under the name of Robert Berman, a professor emeritus at the University of California, Davis. Berman told ABC he had not written the paper and that his research did not make the claims attributed to it. The citation was removed from a revised presentation. Redwood had previously attributed her son’s autism to vaccine-related mercury exposure; that claim conflicts with scientific evidence that vaccines do not cause autism. The episode raised questions about the evidence planned for the advisory meeting. The source account does not specify Redwood’s appointment duties or establish that she held a formal vaccine-safety office, so the title’s description of her role remains unsupported.
